# Plan
**Goal**: small-business finance system, stdlib Python. Full user spec: `.claude/team/spec.md` (read the sections named in your task; follow them exactly).
**Check**: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` (all tests must pass; run only your own test file for quick checks: `python3 -m unittest tests.test_<task>`).

## Contract / Conventions (already written by the lead — READ fin/cli.py, fin/core.py, fin/money.py, fin/db.py, tests/helpers.py first; do not edit them)
- Each task owns ONE module `fin/<task>.py` exposing `register(sub)`; `sub` is the top-level subparsers object. Use `fin.cli.leaf(parent, name, func, access)` for leaf commands, `sub.add_parser("group").add_subparsers(dest="sub", required=True, parser_class=Parser)` for groups (see `_register_core` in fin/cli.py as the model). access = 'read' | 'write' | 'admin' (viewer: read only; editor: read+write; admin: all).
- Handler `def handler(ctx, args)` returns the JSON result exactly as the spec shows (dict/list/str); raise `fin.errors.UserError` for any user error (nothing is committed then). Use `ctx.conn` (sqlite3, row_factory Row, already inside a transaction; never commit).
- Money: Decimal only; `fin.money.fmt()` for every output amount, `round2` rounds half up, `parse_amount/parse_dec/parse_date/parse_month` for input validation, `add_months/add_days/month_end/...` for dates. Amounts stored in DB as decimal strings.
- Post transactions ONLY through `core.post_transaction` (it checks closed periods, balance, accounts). Create accounts with `core.ensure_account`. Every data-changing command calls `core.audit(ctx, action, target)` once (names in spec section 11). Convert currency with `core.convert`/`core.get_rate`. Aggregation helper: `core.balances`.
- DB schema is fixed in fin/db.py (do not change; read comments there). Invoice/bill `lines` JSON = line dicts exactly as shown in the command output.
- Tests: `tests/test_<task>.py`, subclass `tests.helpers.FinCase` (runs the real CLI). Cover every behaviour of your sections incl. error cases (exit 2, empty stdout). Never name a helper `fail`, `run`, `setUp`-like.
- If you find a bug/gap in the lead's shared files, do NOT edit them: describe it in your handoff and work around it.
- Append one line to `.claude/team/changes.md` for any edit outside your own files (you should have none).

## ledger
Owns fin/ledger.py, tests/test_ledger.py. Spec sections 1 (account add/list), 2 (txn add/list), 3 (balance), 4 (fx add, convert). `init`, `user`, `audit`, `period` already exist. `account add` access write; `txn add` write; lists/balance/convert read. Audits: account.add (name — only the named account, once), txn.add (id), fx.add (FROM/TO). Currency codes upper-case 3 letters (validate). Posting parse: `core.parse_posting`. Account `--currency` validation 3 letters. Done check: `python3 -m unittest tests.test_ledger tests.test_core`. Must not touch other files.

## importer
Owns fin/importer.py, tests/test_importer.py. Sections 5 (rule add/list, import), 6 (budget set only — NOT `report budget`), 7 (recurring add/run), 9 (loan schedule; read access, no db change). Import: whole file atomic; check closed period for every row first (post_transaction does it, errors roll back everything); dedupe with table `imported`; category account created via `core.ensure_account` in book currency; ACCOUNT must exist (user error otherwise); rule account must exist at `rule add` time. Import audit target = ACCOUNT; audit even if all skipped. Recurring: postings stored as JSON in `recurring.postings`, validated when added (unknown account/unbalanced -> error; you may validate by building the same checks as post_transaction does, e.g. post nothing: write a small validation using core.get_account and balance check); run generates occurrences start+k months (use add_months from the START date, k=0,1,..) up to --until, skipping ones in `recurring_done`, posting via post_transaction; if any is in a closed period the whole run fails. Budget account must exist and be an expense account. Done check: `python3 -m unittest tests.test_importer`. Must not touch other files.

## sales
Owns fin/sales.py, tests/test_sales.py. Section 13 EXCEPT `report aging` (tax add/list, customer add/list, invoice create/issue/pay/show/list). Needs the ledger commands only for setup in tests (`account add`, `txn add` exist after the ledger task merges; until then insert via `txn`-free setup: tests may create accounts directly with SQL through sqlite3 on self.db, or call `core.ensure_account`; do that rather than depend on ledger). Export a function `invoice_dict(conn, invoice_id)` (used by the API later). Paid = sum of payments rows (kind 'invoice'). Payment must debit an existing asset account. Audit: tax.add (code), customer.add (name), invoice.create/issue/pay (invoice id). Issue number counter: count of already-numbered invoices whose date has the same year, +1. Done check: `python3 -m unittest tests.test_sales`. Must not touch other files.

## purchases
Owns fin/purchases.py, tests/test_purchases.py. Section 14 EXCEPT `report aging --payables` (vendor add/list, bill create/pay/show/list). Same test-setup advice as sales (tax codes: insert into `tax_codes` directly via sqlite3 or `tax add` once sales exists — prefer direct SQL). Export `bill_dict(conn, bill_id)`. Audit: vendor.add, bill.create, bill.pay (bill id). Done check: `python3 -m unittest tests.test_purchases`. Must not touch other files.

## reports
Owns fin/reports.py, tests/test_reports.py. The `report` command group and all subcommands: income, balance-sheet, networth (section 8), budget (section 6), aging incl. `--payables` (sections 13/14; reads tables invoices/bills/payments directly), tax (15), trial-balance, ledger (17); plus `reconcile` (16, write access, audit target = account). Put shared amount aggregation/conversion in helper functions in your file. Conversion: convert each (account, currency) own-balance to target currency with `core.convert` at the report date, then sum per name; missing rate -> UserError. Include accounts only when they have postings in range. Tests set up data through the CLI (`txn add`, `account add`; sales/purchases/ledger modules may not exist yet while you work — for those, seed tables with sqlite3 directly, and for ledger commands use `core.ensure_account` + `core.post_transaction` against a db created by `self.init()`). Done check: `python3 -m unittest tests.test_reports`. Must not touch other files.

## api  (wave 2)
Owns fin/api.py, tests/test_api.py. Section 10 + 11 for HTTP. Command `serve --port N` (access 'serve'-style: register with leaf(..., access="read") then set_defaults access="serve" is NOT allowed — instead use access "read" and block in handler with `http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), Handler).serve_forever()`; main prints nothing special because the handler never returns; flush). Every request is executed via `fin.cli.run(db, user, argv)` (builds argv for the equivalent CLI command, e.g. POST /transactions -> ["txn","add","--date",..,"--desc",..,"--posting","ACC=AMT",...]) in-process, per request; UserError -> `e.status` (400/401/403) with {"error": msg}; POST requires X-User header (missing -> 401) — check role via run(). Unknown path -> 404, bad JSON -> 400. Use `e.status` from AuthError/PermError. Run tests against a real server started in a thread/subprocess on a free port. Endpoints: all in spec section 10 (GET /accounts, /transactions, /balances?at, /reports/income, /reports/balance-sheet, /invoices, /invoices/ID, /reports/aging?at&payables=1, /audit; POST /transactions (201), /invoices (201), /invoices/ID/issue (200), /invoices/ID/payments (200)). Done check: `python3 -m unittest tests.test_api`. Must not touch other files.
